purpose: Lock the ROM-backed player jump and landing VM ordering against a synchronized MAME replay.

replay.command: python tools/oa.py regression player-jump --field terrain.landing_state --field terrain.vertical_stop --field terrain.response_timer_state --field terrain.response_active --field player.animation_pc --field player.frame_ptr

run_stream_compare.operation: F4 compares FFF0CC with zero and branches to idle when equal
run_stream_compare.observed_failure: The native context was captured before ground movement raised FFF0CC, so frame 9 incorrectly returned to 0x00121D9A.
run_stream_compare.observed_fix: Publish post-ground-handler response and horizontal selector values before the player VM tick.

jump_stream_selection.observed_boundary: The jump handler clears FFF0CC before selecting the ordinary root; the launch state must expose 0x001221B2 after the common VM pass.
jump_stream_selection.observed_fix: Select direct locomotion jumps before the VM pass and select landing only after contour-grounded state is latched.

landing_response.observed_sequence: landing_state 1 at launch, 0 on the first airborne pass, 0xFF in the falling phase; vertical_stop 0xFF at residual-upward stop, then 1 after the jump stream writes FFF0C0=1.
landing_response.observed_fix: Model the delayed landing latch and falling phase, and propagate ROM VM ED writes for FFF0C0/FFF0C1 into Engine state.

conclusion: The native player jump, terrain latches, frame pointers, and animation cursors match the MAME replay for all 157 ordinary-jump and 257 timed terrain-jump synchronized frames. The corrected boundaries are ROM/data-backed and protected by CTest differential regressions.
next_action: Use the same earliest-divergence method on the next gameplay or actor-table mismatch; retain the player-jump regression as a gate for future VM and terrain changes.
